To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure function of a passive scalar in a two-dimensional flow is determined by the fractal dimension of the graph of the scalar and the structure function of the flow.

the structure function of a passive scalar in 2D turbulence is a function of the Prandtol number, that it is related to the velocity structure function, and that it is different in the enstrophy and energy inertial subranges.

the fractal dimension of the passive-scalars graph is related to the scaling exponent of the passive-scarlar structure function and the structure function of the underlying flow and that the fractal-dimension of the passive-salr graphs is a function of the Prandt number and the scaling exponent of velocity structure function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scaling properties of the scalar passive advection.
the structure functions of the passive-scalars in two-dimensional (2D) turbulence and the fractal dimension of the scalar graphs.
the scaling behavior of the passive-scalars structure function and its graph in 2D turbulence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in 2D, there is no universal behavior of the scalar structure functions, and that the exponent of D1(r) depends on the driving of the scalar field.
the fractal dimension of the passive-scalars graph is a function of the driving of that passive scalar, the Prandtl-number, and of the underlying 2D turbulent flow.
the fractal dimension of the scalar field depends on the scaling exponent of the flow field and the Prandtl-number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the passive-scalar scaling exponent zeta(1)(theta) is not a universal quantity, and that the scaling exponent delta1g of passive-scalar graphs is related to the scaling of the velocity structure function.
the 2D passive scalar is a more complex object than its 3D counterpart.
the passive scalar graph is a more appropriate quantity to study the scaling of passive scalar fields than the scalar structure function itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fractal dimension of the passive-scar graph is a powerful tool to study the passive-scalar dynamics and to discriminate between different scalings in the 2D case.
, in contrast to 3D turbulence, the structure function of a passive scalar in 2D turbulence is not universal.
the passive scalar structure function depends on the driving of the underlying flow and not only on the flow field itself.
